[tool_result Bash] # Twin — Roadmap

Oct 4, 2026 · @Meir Kanevskiy

Twin is an orthodox two-pane commander at roughly mc-1995 feature level, wrapped in a clean Bubble Tea MVU codebase. The skeleton is good enough to build on; the file-operation layer is not yet safe to trust with real data.

## Where Twin stands today

**What works:** two panes with Tab switching; arrow/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn navigation; `..` parent entry with cursor restored on the way up; Insert to select; copy, move, delete, mkdir with a y/n/All/skip-all overwrite prompt; copy path to clipboard with an OSC 52 fallback; a plain-text preview (100 KB cap, binary detection); a favorites + mounted-drives popup with unmount; sync panes (Alt+I) and open-dir-in-other-pane (Alt+O); xdg-open on Enter; prefix-then-fuzzy quick search; an Alt hint bar.

**What's good about the architecture:**

- The file split by responsibility (model / update / commands / msg / fs / keys / view / styles) is clean and easy to navigate.
- All I/O already lives in `tea.Cmd` closures that return messages, so the UI never blocks and there is a natural seam for a job engine.
- Keys go through a `KeyMap` with canonical Alt bindings plus F-key aliases, so remapping and presets are a small step away.
- `focusPath` on reload is the right primitive for keeping the cursor where the user expects it.

**What will hurt as it grows:**

- Modal state is a chain of mutually exclusive booleans in one \~600-line `Update`. Every new dialog adds a branch and a chance to forget a guard (one is already missing; see below).
- `pane` is a plain struct with no notion of a data source, so archives, SFTP, search results or a tree view would each need special cases.
- No config, no persistence (favorites vanish on exit), no tests, and `m.err` is set in many places but never rendered.
- It's on Bubble Tea v1 while emitting a raw Kitty keyboard escape in `main.go`. Charm shipped v2 of Bubble Tea, Lip Gloss and Bubbles in February 2026 ([release notes](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/releases)), and v2 handles keyboard enhancements, modifier events and OSC 52 natively.
- DOCUMENTATION.md has drifted: it says Alt+I / Ctrl+I select files, but Alt+I is Sync Panes, Ctrl+I is indistinguishable from Tab in most terminals, and selection is actually Insert.

## Fix first: bugs found reading the code

Three of these can destroy data today, so they come before any feature work. All were found by reading the source, not by running it; each deserves a regression test when fixed.

| Severity | Where | What happens | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | `update.go` Delete / Copy / Move, `fs.go` `readDirectory` | The synthetic `..` entry is a real target. The cursor sits on `..` (index 0) after every directory change, so Alt+D then `y` runs `os.RemoveAll` on the **parent directory**. Insert can also select `..`. | Mark `..` as a pseudo-entry (`IsParent bool`), exclude it from selection and from every operation's fallback-to-cursor. |
| Critical | `update.go` overwrite loop, `processOverwriteConflicts` | Pressing `y` (or `n`) on the first conflict calls `processOverwriteConflicts()` immediately, which force-copies **all remaining** conflicts. Answering `n` to file 1 silently overwrites files 2..N. | Turn conflict resolution into an explicit queue: one decision per file, apply only decided items, then advance. |
| Critical | `commands.go` `copyFilesCmd` / `moveFilesCmd` | If any file conflicts, the command returns before copying anything; resolution only re-runs the conflicting files. Non-conflicting files in the batch are silently dropped. | Plan the whole batch first (conflicts + clean items), resolve, then execute everything. |
| High | `update.go` favorites branch + final delegation guard | The guard before `pane.update` omits `isFavoritesOpen`, so up/down move both the popup and the pane, and `d`, `j`, `k`, `q` leak into quick search. | Replace the boolean chain with a modal stack whose top always consumes input. |
| High | `commands.go` `moveFilesCmd` | `os.Rename` fails with EXDEV across filesystems, so moving to a USB drive (a featured use case) always errors. Renaming onto a non-empty dir also fails. | Fallback to copy + verify + delete on EXDEV; merge semantics for directories. |
| High | `fs.go` `copyDir` | Copying a directory into itself recurses forever; symlinks are followed (loops, and links become copies); mtimes are not preserved. | Reject dest-inside-source; copy symlinks as symlinks by default; preserve mode + mtime. |
| High | everywhere `m.err` is set | Errors are stored but never rendered, so a failed copy or delete looks like success. | Toast/notification area plus an error log (`Ctrl+L` or similar). |
| Medium | mkdir input, quick search | `len(msg.String()) == 1` counts bytes, so Hebrew, Russian or any non-ASCII letter is dropped; backspace slices bytes and can corrupt UTF-8. Paste is ignored. | Use `bubbles/textinput` for every text field; match on runes. |
| Medium | `main.go` | Kitty keyboard flags `15` (including report-all-keys-as-escapes) are enabled by hand, but Bubble Tea v1 can't parse CSI-u. On terminals that honor it, plain letters may arrive as garbage. | Remove now; let Bubble Tea v2 negotiate keyboard enhancements. |
| Medium | `commands.go` `previewFileCmd` | `os.ReadFile` loads the whole file before the 100 KB check, so previewing a multi-GB file reads it all. The cut can land mid-rune. | Open, read the first N KB, trim to a rune boundary. |
| Low | `view.go` `statusBarView` | `status[:availableWidth]` slices bytes and panics if the width goes negative on a tiny terminal. Long names and paths are never truncated in panes. | Width-aware truncation with an ellipsis (`ansi.Truncate`). |
| Low | `update.go` `fileDeletedMsg` | Cursor is adjusted against the old file list before the reload arrives. | Restore position by neighbouring path via `focusPath`. |

## Vision: the orthodox commander, modernized

Twin should be to mc what eza is to ls: the same mental model and muscle memory, with good defaults, rich information and zero required configuration.

## Milestones and what to build next

Each phase ships as a tagged release, so Twin is usable (and dogfoodable) from v0.1 onward.

[embedded content: release path · 9 phases, v0.1 to v1.0\]

Phases 0 to 4 run in order; preview, shell and virtual filesystems can be built in any order once the commander core lands, and all three feed 1.0.

**The first three PRs:**

1. Make `..` a pseudo-entry excluded from all operations; replace the conflict loop with a per-file queue and plan whole batches before executing. Add `fs_test.go` covering each case.
2. Render errors (toast + log) and move mkdir and search input to `bubbles/textinput` so non-ASCII names work.
3. On a branch: Bubble Tea v2 migration together with the modal stack, since both rewrite the top of `Update` anyway.
